column1: # Differences between kyo-email's reading of an unstructured field and Stalwart mail-parser's, over resources/unstructured.json
# Kept by hand: HeaderCodecTest prints, in this format, each row missing here and each row here that no longer occurs.
# Columns, tab-separated: vector index from 0, header, the module's value, Stalwart's value, reason. Backslash, tab, CR and LF
# in a value are written as \\, \t, \r and \n, and any other control character as \uXXXX.
# Reasons, each the first rule of HeaderCodecStalwart.classify that holds:

#   WhiteSpaceInEncodedText: Stalwart decodes a =?...?= span whose encoded text holds white space, written in or left by a fold; RFC 2047 sections 2 and 5 forbid it, and the module keeps each piece as text

#   SpaceInsertedBesideWord: Both decode an encoded word joined to other text with no white space between them; Stalwart rebuilds the white space around it as single spaces, which inserts one there, and the module keeps the text as written, as CPython's email.policy.default parser does
#   FoldWhiteSpaceCollapsed: Stalwart replaces a fold and the white space around it with one space; RFC 5322 section 2.2.3 removes only the line end, and the module keeps the white space
